limitations: Stage E.2 is synthetic, sandboxed, and small.
Domain and policy comparisons are descriptive only.
Prevention claims require matched no-oversight support.
required_report_statements: Stage E.2 uses synthetic tasks, synthetic constraints, and inert tools.
No real sensitive data is used.
No real external action is performed.
The attacker receives no hidden labels, scorer rules, monitor thresholds, or benchmark answers.
The matrix was selected before provider outcomes were observed.
Monitor parameters and thresholds remain frozen.
The sample is small and cannot estimate population prevalence.
Results do not establish broad real-world attacker robustness.
Domain, architecture, attacker-family, and policy comparisons are descriptive.
Positive-case performance is measured only when objective-positive trajectories actually occur.
Prevention claims apply only to objectively preventable matched cases.
scientific_framing: Stage E.2 is a small, controlled, synthetic, sandboxed strategic-attacker pilot. It evaluates attack success, objective violations, monitor detection, oversight intervention, and prevention under the frozen Stage E.1 design.
